values.title: Where I am most useful
values.intro: I join a team for one product problem at a time, usually for six to twelve weeks, and work directly with engineers and the people who use the product.

items.title: Product direction
items.text: Turning a vague brief into a clear problem, a plan and a first prototype within two weeks.

items.title: Research with users
items.text: Interviews and field visits with the people who use the product, not only the people who buy it.

items.title: Interaction design
items.text: Flows and screens for web and mobile, tested with users before anyone writes code.

items.title: Design systems
items.text: Components, tokens and documentation your team can keep up after I leave.

items.title: Prototyping
items.text: Clickable prototypes in Figma, or coded ones when timing and motion matter.

items.title: Handover to engineering
items.text: Specs, edge cases and empty states written down, with time set aside for questions during the build.

values.title: Selected projects, 2022 to 2026
values.text: Five projects from my own studio and my years at Kvist. Each starts with the problem, then what I did and what changed after launch. The numbers come from each client’s own reporting.

values.title: Renting a bike in 19 seconds, with one hand
values.text: Havn runs 4,200 shared bikes and scooters in Copenhagen, Aarhus and Malmö. One in four rentals was abandoned between scanning the bike and unlocking it. Over 14 weeks I interviewed riders at stations, cut the rental flow from seven screens to three and saw it through release with four engineers.

items.text: Unlock time down from 48 to 19 seconds
Abandoned rentals down from 24 to 9 percent
App Store rating up from 3.6 to 4.6 in four months
Released in all three cities in June 2026

image.alt: The new Havn unlock screen on a phone clipped to a bike handlebar

values.quote: We had tried to fix the rental flow twice before. Maren was the first person to ask riders where they hold their phone while they unlock a bike. That one question changed the whole design.
values.result: Completed rentals up from 76 to 91 percent
values.name: Jesper Lund

values.title: A clinic calendar physiotherapists can run between patients
values.text: Tolva sells booking software to 140 physiotherapy clinics in Denmark and Norway. Receptionists juggled the calendar while patients called to book. For five months, two days a week, I redesigned the calendar and the patient booking flow, and set up the design system the team now runs on its own.

items.text: Online bookings up from 41 to 63 percent
No-shows down 22 percent after new reminders
64 components handed over to Tolva’s own team

image.alt: A clinic’s week view in the new Tolva calendar on a reception desk monitor

values.title: Three more projects
values.intro: A freight dispatch board, a design system for four products and the savings feature I led at Kvist.

rows.title: Morrow Freight: a dispatch board for planners who lived in spreadsheets
rows.text: Thirty planners in Hamburg and Aarhus assign 900 loads a day. I sat with them for three shifts, then designed a board around how they already worked. The spreadsheet was retired eight weeks after launch in January 2026, and planners now handle 30 percent more loads per shift.

image.alt: The Morrow dispatch board showing trucks, loads and delivery windows on a timeline

rows.title: Ferro: one design system for four invoicing products
rows.text: Ferro’s four products had drifted into four styles. Over ten weeks in 2025 I built a shared system of 180 components with their designers and engineers. A new feature now takes two weeks to design instead of six.

image.alt: A Ferro design system page showing buttons, form fields and their states

rows.title: Kvist: savings goals that customers finish
rows.text: As lead product designer at Kvist, I redesigned savings goals for 1.8 million customers. Clearer progress and automatic transfers raised goal completion by 31 percent in 2022.

image.alt: A Kvist savings goal screen showing progress towards a summer holiday fund

values.title: Have a product that needs this kind of attention?
Eleven years of product design, three on my own
values.text: I spent three years at a Copenhagen design studio and five leading design at Kvist. Since 2023 I have worked for myself from a small studio in Nørrebro.

image.alt: Portrait of Maren Holt in her studio, standing by a wall of printed screens

values.title: How I got here
values.lead: The short version: a studio, then one product for five years, then my own practice. The longer version explains why I work the way I do.
values.body:
I started at Nordlys, a digital studio in Copenhagen, designing ticket machines and booking sites for transport companies in Denmark and Sweden. Three years of short projects taught me to find the real problem quickly, and that most of it sits outside the screen.

Five years inside one product

In 2018 I joined Kvist as its second designer. By 2023 I led a team of six, working on payments, savings and the design system every Kvist screen is still built on. Staying with one product that long taught me what studios rarely see: what happens to a design two years after launch.

Why I went independent

I wanted to work on more kinds of problems without losing that depth. So I take two clients at a time, stay for at least six weeks and work inside the team, rather than handing over a deck at the end.

  • Banking, health, mobility and logistics software
  • Product teams of 3 to 30 people
  • On site in Copenhagen, Aarhus or Malmö, remote anywhere in Europe

Outside client work

Each spring I teach a six-week course on designing public services, and I mentor two junior designers a year.

values.title: Four steps, on every project

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Week one: interviews with your team and the people who use the product. You get a one-page brief with the problem we agree to solve.

steps.title: Sketch and test
steps.text: Weeks two to four: paper and clickable prototypes, tested with five to eight users in each round.

steps.title: Design and specify
steps.text: Final screens, states and edge cases, built on your design system or a new one we set up together.

steps.title: Ship together
steps.text: I stay through the build, review every release candidate and measure the results after launch.

values.title: Three ways to work with me

cards.title: Project
cards.text: Six to twelve weeks on one product problem, from research to handover. A fixed fee, agreed after a free scoping call.

cards.title: Design partner
cards.text: Two days a week inside your team for three months or more. For teams that do not have a senior designer yet.

cards.title: Design review
cards.text: One day with your product and your team, then a written review with clear priorities. €1,900, fixed.

values.title: Send me a short brief
values.text: A few lines are enough: what the product is, who uses it, what is not working and when you would like to start.
values.messageLabel: What are you working on, and when would you like to start?

values.title: Rates and availability
values.text: Something else you would like to know? Ask me directly.

items.question: What does a project cost?
items.answer: Most projects are a fixed fee, agreed after a free 30-minute scoping call. As a guide, a six-week project costs between €26,000 and €34,000. For smaller pieces of work my day rate is €950, excluding VAT.

items.question: When are you available?
items.answer: I am booking projects that start from 2 November 2026. I work with two clients at a time, so a short brief now helps me hold a slot for you.

items.question: Do you work on site or remotely?
items.answer: Both. I am happy to spend one or two days a week with your team in Copenhagen, Aarhus or Malmö, and I work remotely with teams anywhere in Europe.

items.question: Do you work with agencies?
items.answer: Yes, as the senior product designer on an agency team, as long as I can talk directly to the client’s users and engineers.

items.question: What do you need from us to start?
items.answer: A product owner who can make decisions, access to the people who use the product and one engineer I can ask questions. Everything else we set up in the first week.

items.question: Will you sign an NDA?
items.answer: Yes. I sign NDAs as standard, and I only show client work on this site with written permission.
